episodes.158302: Very warm and humid airmass across the region on te afternoon of June 29th. One thunderstorm that developed across the southern Adirondacks during the afternoon quickly intensified in the northern Hudson Valley near Granville and then moved southeast across Pawlet in Rutland county before proceeding into Bennington county. One isolated report of tree down across utility lines along Route 30.
episodes.158313: A strong high pressure center over the Pacific Northwest pulled in moisture from the east which produced thunderstorms over the Sierra Nevada during the afternoon of June 29.  Although the thunderstorms on the previous day were mainly dry with very little rainfall, the moisture surge the following day was deeper and as a result some of the thunderstorms produced locally heavy rainfall, damaging outflow winds and small hail during the afternoon and early evening hours of June 29.
episodes.158326: Thunderstorms moving across coastal waters produce strong wind gusts.
episodes.158392: Scattered thunderstorms moved across northwest Indiana during the afternoon of June 29th producing localized severe winds.
episodes.158448: During the evening hours of June 29th, isolated to scattered thunderstorms were moving across much of central Indiana.  Later in the evening, a few thunderstorms across southeastern Indiana interacted with a local boundary that was enough to grow the storms large enough for brief damaging wind and hail to occur.
episodes.158469: Thunderstorms that developed in the late afternoon hours of June 28 produced wind gusts that brought down numerous trees and power lines across parts of East Tennessee.
episodes.158476: A warm and humid airmass across the Ohio Valley resulted in scattered thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening hours.
episodes.158488: Near record hot temperatures and increasing moisture led to the development of scattered slow moving thunderstorms with heavy rainfall.
episodes.158809: An upper level low anchored over the Gulf of Mexico conintued to pull deep tropical moisture across South Florida. As daytime heating increased, showers and thunderstorms developed over the Atlantic waters. A few of these storms became strong enough to produce gusty winds and waterspouts off shore Key Biscayne and Fischer Island.
episodes.158832: A push of monsoon moisture fueled thunderstorms over northwest Arizona. One storm produced flash flooding.
episodes.158841: The Southeast Alaska region saw well above normal snowpack through out the 2020-2021 winter, recording between 175 to 200% of normal snow water equivalent. There was a delay in snowmelt in the spring time due to cooler than normal temperatures in April and May to keep larger river's stream flows below normal. Temperatures started to be closer to normal in the second half of the first week of June over Southeast Alaska which began to prime the snowpack in larger rivers basins like the Taku River which originates in British Columbia, Canada.  The Taku River started to see rise from the snow melt from the primed snowpack. Then the region was hit by an atmospheric river which produced moderate rainfall along with high freezing level to significantly increase the ripening process of the snowpack not just over Southeast Alaska but also over northern British Columbia. After the atmospheric river moved through Southeast Alaska a very anomalous heat wave hit British Columbia and Southeast Alaska with record temperatures in the 90s to 100 degrees. The very warm day and night time temperatures produced above normal river levels and daily record streams on the Taku River from the snowmelt. This perfect storm produced record flooding along the Taku River after a glacier dammed lake along the Tulseqhuah Glacier, Lake No Lake, drained. Areas around the Taku River were flooded with homes and cabins getting moderately impacted. The Taku River crested at 45.5ft which was above major flood stage of 45ft and bested the old record stage of 45.07ft from 2004.
episodes.158980: Small clusters of thunderstorms moved north to northwest around the periphery of a 500 mb high centered off the Carolina coast. At the surface, a weak cold front trailed southwest from Lake Michigan to the Ozarks. A few isolated strong wind gusts accompanied the strongest storms during the heat of the afternoon.
episodes.158981: Small clusters of thunderstorms moved north to northwest around the periphery of a 500 mb high centered off the Carolina coast. At the surface, a weak cold front trailed southwest from Lake Michigan to the Ozarks. A few isolated strong wind gusts accompanied the strongest storms during the heat of the afternoon.
episodes.158983: The Mississippi River rose above flood stage at Cape Girardeau just before the end of the month. Minor flooding of low-lying fields occurred.
episodes.159071: Oppressive heat and humidity and strong low level lapse rates created the environment for scattered severe thunderstorms to form in the late afternoon and evening hours across portions of Massachusetts and northern Connecticut.
episodes.159072: Oppressive heat and humidity and strong low level lapse rates created the environment for scattered severe thunderstorms to form in the late afternoon and evening hours across portions of Massachusetts and northern Connecticut.
episodes.159434: Northern Ohio was in the warm sector during the afternoon through early evening of the 29th as a surface low moved from the Upper Mississippi Valley toward the western Upper Peninsula of Michigan. Simultaneously, the Bermuda-Azores subtropical high extended a weak ridge over the Upper Ohio Valley and eastern Great Lakes region. Numerous thunderstorms developed along the Lake Erie lake breeze front and via daytime heating farther inland, amidst a warm and very humid boundary layer. These storms occurred in an environment with moderate to strong instability and DCAPE, and weak to moderate vertical wind shear.
episodes.159513: Scattered severe thunderstorms moved across eastern New York resulting in trees and powerlines down during the afternoon and evening of the 29th. As a result of the storms, there were 15,000 homes without power in Greene and Columbia counties.
episodes.159649: A very moist airmass and slow moving storms led to a multi-day heavy rainfall event for much of the area. 6 to 8+ inches fell in a swath from southwest OK northeast along the I-44 corridor. Several storms also produced isolated severe weather with hail and strong winds reported.
episodes.159656: Slow moving thunderstorms embedded in a stagnant, hot and humid airmass produced torrential rainfall and urban flooding in the Syracuse, NY area.
episodes.159737: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed across Middle Tennessee during the morning to early afternoon hours on June 29th. A few storms became severe with damaging winds.
episodes.159794: For the second time in less than a week, storms producing locally heavy rains moved across Crawford County in southwest Wisconsin. The runoff from the rain caused standing high water, mud and rock slides that closed a portion of State Highway 35 west of Eastman. Radar estimates indicated up to 3 inches of rain fell on ground that was already saturated.
episodes.159795: Storms with locally heavy rains moved across portions of northeast Iowa on June 29th. These storms dumped around 3 inches of rain over eastern Allamakee County that resulted in some flash flooding. Mud slides and flooded roads were reported in the vicinity of Waukon Junction and water went over several roads in the Yellow River State Forest.
episodes.159882: Scattered severe thunderstorms moved across western New England resulting in downed trees during the afternoon and evening of the 29th.
episodes.159884: Scattered severe thunderstorms moved across western New England resulting in downed trees during the afternoon and evening of the 29th.
episodes.159902: Moisture and warm air due to southwest winds helped provide the support needed for scattered thunderstorms across Central New York. Many storms became severe, producing strong, damaging winds. There were numerous reports of trees and utility wires knocked down, often onto roadways which then resulted in closed roadways.
episodes.160037: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with scattered afternoon thunderstorms across the tri-state region. There were a few reports of wind damage with the strongest storms.
episodes.160038: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with scattered afternoon thunderstorms across the tri-state region. There were a few reports of wind damage with the strongest storms.
episodes.160072: An upper level low pressure system was over the Arizona and New Mexico border. There was a stationary front across the area which provided additional lift over West Texas. Abundant moisture was continuing to move into the region. These conditions resulted in rain and thunderstorms developing and moving over the same areas producing flash flooding across West Texas.
episodes.160136: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with a few strong thunderstorms producing wind gusts in excess of 34 knots.
episodes.160144: During the afternoon on June 29, the southeastern United States was in an area of high pressure. In the weak shear environment, pulse thunderstorms initiated during the warming of the day. Outflow boundaries, from the first storms, initiated other storms. This resulted in isolated wind damage to trees and power lines across south-central Indiana.
episodes.160173: Monsoon moisture increasing from the south brought thunderstorms across northern Arizona. The outflow boundary form one of the thunderstorms produced a landspout tornado over Doney Park.
episodes.160204: Flash flooding occurred across portions of the Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument, in Zion National Park, and in the town of Hilldale.
episodes.160227: An upper level low pressure was to the west of the region which aided in atmospheric lift over Southeast New Mexico. Convergence was also over the area which allowed for more lift. An abundance of moisture was in place. These conditions resulted in flash flooding across Eddy County.
episodes.160282: A stalled out surface low across the area lead to a week of conditions favorable for funnel cloud development. In the afternoon and evening hours of June 25, 26, 27, 29, and 30, funnel clouds were reported across Iowa. 0-3 km CAPE values around 100 J/kg and surface vorticity in the vicinity of the surface low made for a good funnel cloud environment for several days, though there was no report of any tornadic activity with any showers.
episodes.160358: Strong surface heating with temperatures in the 90s and dewpoints in the 70s resulted in sufficient destabilization for storms to form, specifically along lake breeze boundaries in the middle to late afternoon. A Heat Advisory was in effect for lower elevations excluding Jefferson County. Surface based instability was strong and precipitable water values were almost 2 inches. Shear was minimal across most of the region with 20-25 knots across western New York increasing to 30-35 knots across Lake Ontario and the North Country. The strongest shear was across southern Ontario, north of Lake Ontario, where widespread convection was occurring by early afternoon. A few storms were able to capitalize on lake breeze boundaries to the south of the Buffalo Metro area with isolated damage in southern Erie County and Wyoming County.
episodes.160395: An unseasonably hot and humid airmass was firmly in place across the state with high instability values.  Most of the convection was capped through the day, but a few isolated storms were able to develop on the evening of the 29th.  An isolated storm became severe in the Connecticut River Valley north of Lebanon.
episodes.160456: Thunderstorms developing during the afternoon hours and produced gusty winds that caused damage in the Florida panhandle.
episodes.160469: During the afternoon on June 29, the southeastern United States was in an area of high pressure. In the weak shear environment, pulse thunderstorms initiated during the warming of the day. Outflow boundaries, from the first storms, initiated other storms. This resulted in isolated wind damage to trees and power lines near Bowling Green.
episodes.160483: Scattered thunderstorms developed as several outflow boundaries interacted with an unstable and moderately sheared environment. A few of the storms produced marginally severe wind gusts.
episodes.160523: Several severe thunderstorms produced wind damage,  between the I-69 and I-94 corridors.
episodes.160534: Thunderstorms moving into Lake St. Clair produced wind gusts around 35 knots.

episodes.160574: Heavy rain caused some minor flooding near Graham.
episodes.160618: A band of showers and thunderstorms associated with the remnants of Tropical Storm Danny pushed into West Tennessee during the afternoon hours of June 29, 2021. A few severe storms with damaging winds occurred.
episodes.160633: The accelerated lower tropospheric flow between the Bermuda-Azores High across the western Atlantic and a tropical wave passing to the south-southwest of the Florida Keys resulted in numerous showers and thunderstorms.  A few gale-force wind gusts were measured.

The Taku River water levels were at record daily stream flows hovering just below minor flooding stage of 43 feet by the end on July from well above normal snowpack, delayed snowmelt from a cool spring and then rapid snowmelt from impacts of an atmospheric river and then record high temperatures. One the morning of June 29th the public reported that the glacier dammed lake, Lake No Lake, on the Tulsequah Glacier just over the Canadian boarder was starting to release water into Tulsequah River which is a tributary to the Taku River. The Taku River started to rise steadily for the next 36 hours as the Lake No Lake totally drained. There was about 50,000 cubic feet per second of water added to the Taku River from Lake No Lake and combined with record daily stream flows already occurring on the Taku River it produced record flooding going above the previous record of 45.07 feet from 2004. A number of homes were affected from the moderate to major flooding with water in homes and some foundations being compromised.
